title: Do You Know the Critical Set of Technical Skills or Actions Required for Your Best Performance
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article contends that mastery in any field depends on precisely identifying the small set of technical skills that actually drive top performance -- not just practicing broadly. While sports have well-established playbooks for which skills matter most, the author notes that most business roles lack this clarity, leaving practitioners guessing at what to master. The recommended fix is gathering experienced practitioners together to hash out a specific short list, then designing deliberate practice around it. The piece closes with a Vince Lombardi quote reinforcing that only 'perfect practice' -- practice targeted at the right skills -- produces real gains.
points: Great performance rests on mastering a specific, identifiable set of technical skills, not vague general effort.
Business roles often lack the established skill inventories that sports have, making it harder to know what to practice.
Leaders should convene experienced practitioners to define a concrete short list of the skills that matter most for a given role.
Practice sessions should be deliberately designed around that list rather than left general or unfocused.
quotes: Great performers and performances depend on the near-perfect execution of a specific set of technical skills.
Top performers strive to execute the technical skills in the same precise way over and over, without thinking about them.
Perhaps the biggest challenge many performers face is not the practice, but rather identifying exactly what technical skills they must master.
By engaging with experts and top performers in any role, they create a short list of those actions and skills most important to top performance.
In the words of legendary coach Vince Lombardi, “Practice doesn’t make perfect. Only perfect practice makes perfect.
